Why pixel art needs whole-number scaling

Pixel art looks crisp only when every source pixel becomes the same number of screen pixels. When a game scales by 2.5, some pixels become two wide and some become three, and the art starts to shimmer as the camera moves.

The fix is simple: draw the game at a small base resolution, then scale it by a whole number like 2, 3 or 4. Add black bars, or a soft border, for the leftover space instead of stretching the picture.

Turn off smoothing

Browsers smooth images by default, which blurs pixel art into mush. Set image-rendering to pixelated on the canvas, and turn off image smoothing in the 2D context, so edges stay sharp at every size.

We decided to lock our game at 320 by 180 pixels, because it scales cleanly to 1280 by 720 and 1920 by 1080, the two most common screens our players use.

Next, we need to test the scaling on phones, where odd screen sizes make whole-number scaling leave larger borders.

  • Pick one base resolution early.
  • Scale by whole numbers only.
  • Keep text in the same pixel grid as the art.
